proposed_from.topic: Exact second-order minimax excess-risk frontier for a linear causal functional in a sequential (non-anticipating) experiment, over the UNRESTRICTED estimator class. Setting: K >= 2 arms, X in [0,1]^d, latent units (X, Y(1),...,Y(K)) i.i.d., observed data generated by any non-anticipating design (Li and Simchi-Levi arXiv:2606.31190 Definition 2.1) with positivity floor eps; no interference; target theta(P) = E[sum_a omega_a(X) mu_a(X)] with fixed known bounded weights (contains ATE, weighted/subgroup ATE, policy value). Model class P(s,r): fixed n-independent Holder class -- covariate density bounded above and below on [0,1]^d, Gaussian conditional outcomes, mu_a in H^s(L_mu) with sup-norm bound M, sigma_a^2 in H^r(L_sig) with values in [v_min, v_max]; so the nuisance L2 minimax exponents are alpha = s/(2s+d) for the outcome regressions and beta = r/(2r+d) for the design-relevant second moments m_a = omega_a^2 sigma_a^2, both automatically in (0,1/2). Define R_n(s,r) := inf over pairs (non-anticipating design, ANY F_n-measurable estimator T) of sup over P in P(s,r) of { E_P[(T - theta(P))^2] - V*(P)/n }, where V*(P) is the oracle generalized-Neyman semiparametric benchmark inf_e V(e) at P; the loss is MEAN-SQUARED ERROR and NO unbiasedness, regularity, asymptotic-linearity or bias-rate restriction is imposed on T. CONJECTURE: R_n(s,r) is of exact order max( n^{-1-2alpha}, n^{-1-2beta} ) with matching bounds up to constants only, with NO logarithmic factor on either side. This settles two things the anchor leaves open: (i) its Theorem 4.6 converse holds only for EXACTLY unbiased estimators, because its whole proof runs through the Cauchy-projection identity Var_P(T) - V*(P)/n = E_P[(T - theta_oracle)^2] (Lemma E.5), which substitutes E_P[T] = theta(P) exactly and whose variance criterion is vacuous for biased T -- and the anchor's o(n^{-1/2}) bias relaxation (Remark 3.2) is a FIRST-order relaxation, useless at the second-order scale n^{-1/2-alpha}; (ii) both halves are stated only up to logarithmic factors. Mechanics DELEGATED to the solver: the converse mechanism, all constants, the batching schedule, sample-splitting scheme and nuisance learners, whether the attaining pair is the anchor's batched cross-fitted procedure or a modification, any log-removal argument, and whether Gaussianity can be relaxed to sub-Gaussian.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest second-order upper result is Li and Simchi-Levi's Section 4.4 Theorem 4.6, equations (16)--(18), which is an oracle-subtracted MSE bound for their batched cross-fitted pair but remains \(\widetilde O\)-slack. Theorem 4.7, equation (19), says ``for any non-anticipating experiment and unbiased estimator pair'' and concerns oracle-subtracted variance up to logarithmic factors. Appendix F, Lemma F.6, equation (78), assumes local unbiasedness and uses \(E_P[T]=\theta(P)\) in its proof. The unrestricted assertion is strictly stronger because one law-independent kernel class and one common measurable estimator class are fixed before the supremum over \(P\), arbitrary bias is charged by oracle-subtracted MSE, and the same two-scale frontier is proved without logarithmic factors. The closest nuisance theorem is Shen et al.'s univariate variance-function minimax result, which has no causal design or oracle-excess criterion. The additional absorption identity derives why the general-dimensional two-exponent causal frontier survives the unknown-mean variance bottleneck.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Conclusion, Theorem 4.6, Remark 3.2, and Lemma E.5 were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Replace the unbiased projection converse by an unrestricted excess-MSE reduction and remove both logarithmic losses.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is immediate from Theorem 4.6 after replacing variance by MSE. Rebuttal: Lemma E.5 substitutes exact centering, while biased estimators require risk comparison across laws and the benchmark subtraction changes with the law.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, variance-function theorem, proof sketch, discussion, and stated open random-design questions were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Determine whether adaptive generalized Neyman allocation inherits the joint mean--variance minimax bottleneck.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: Shen et al. already give the rate. Rebuttal: their target is a variance function under an i.i.d. regression experiment, not causal excess MSE after joint optimization over adaptive designs and unrestricted estimators.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, multistage competitive theorems, and Conclusions were read from the arXiv source; the conclusion flags the finite-sample proxy-MSE gap and tail risk.
seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Characterize \(\mathsf R_{n,B}\) and the smallest policy-update budget that reaches the unrestricted frontier.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: geometric stages make the answer a routine recursion. Rebuttal: the nonparametric mean and variance risks enter every batch through different exponents, and a matching lower bound must respect the update constraint.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, main MSE comparison, conjectured discrepancy improvement, and concluding discussion were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Derive the exact regime where balancing with a moment estimator matches or diverges from regression-adjusted generalized Neyman design.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: the difference is merely the known online-discrepancy logarithm. Rebuttal: the proposed frontier would separate discrepancy, outcome smoothness, and allocation-learning regimes against a model-dependent oracle.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The banked proposal's open-ended question and its cited Neopane--Ramdas--Singh introduction and conclusion were read; the paper flags AIPW and larger action spaces as future work.
seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Identify and attain the leading curvature--information constant for cumulative Neyman regret.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is the banked proposal unchanged. Rebuttal: it is credible but fails the new-angle novelty requirement and is therefore not selected.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Theorem 1, nonparametric example, and Discussion were read from the PMLR paper.
seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Construct a second-order local asymptotic minimax benchmark that rules out sequential superefficiency after subtracting \(V^*(P)/n\).
seed_details.red_team: Objection: Duchi--Ruan already handles superefficiency. Rebuttal: their inequality does not preserve a law-dependent sequential oracle subtraction or identify its exact Hölder modulus.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, martingale asymptotic-normality section, finite-sample discussion, and Conclusion were read from the arXiv source.
seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Derive a nuisance-sensitive second-order distributional approximation and coverage error for predictable AIPW under learned Neyman allocation.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is a routine Berry--Esseen refinement of a martingale CLT. Rebuttal: the allocation learner changes the conditional variance path and the target is a uniform smoothness-indexed coverage frontier.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The paper's Conclusion was read; it explicitly names heterogeneous treatment effects and dynamic treatment assignment as extensions.
seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Choose a policy from a constrained class using the same adaptive experiment and derive the welfare-regret price of learning the design.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is ordinary doubly robust policy learning under martingale data. Rebuttal: a valid version needs a joint design--policy regret lower bound, but that kernel changes the fixed-estimand target too far for this run.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction and Conclusion were read from the arXiv source; neither supplies a symmetry-based finite-sample route.
seed_details.open_question_leveraged: Invert the known sequential assignment law for finite-sample causal intervals under a sharp null.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: Fisher randomization inversion identifies only sharp nulls and does not deliver the superpopulation linear functional's second-order frontier. Rebuttal: no adequate rebuttal within the stated target, so the seed is dropped.

banked_reason: D0.5 kernel_substituted: the advertised exact unrestricted minimax frontier was replaced by a one-sided log-free upper bound, while the unrestricted centered converse remained open.
banked_proposal_promise_gap: A future proposal must supply an explicit sequential Bayes information-regret lower construction uniform over every non-anticipating design and show cancellation of every law-dependent term in V*(P)/n; fixed-design or ordinary total-risk lower bounds do not suffice.
